title: Salesforce vs. International Business Machines: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
detail:
Salesforce vs. International Business Machines: Which Technology Stock Is a Better Buy in 2026?
Jake Lerch, The Motley Fool
Mon, October 26, 2026 at 11:50 AM EDT 6 min read
CRM
IBM
Explore stocks on Coinbase
Trading disclosure

Choosing between Salesforce (NYSE:CRM) and International Business Machines (NYSE:IBM) in 2026 requires balancing the high-growth potential of a cloud software leader against the steady reliability of a diversified technology veteran.

Salesforce dominates the software landscape by helping companies manage customer data through the cloud. IBM has transformed itself into a specialist in hybrid cloud and consulting. Both companies are now competing for enterprise dollars by embedding artificial intelligence into their core service offerings.

The case for Salesforce

Salesforce sells a comprehensive suite of cloud-based tools that allow companies to manage sales, customer service, and marketing on a single platform. The business focuses on driving adoption across its various software modules, particularly among large enterprise clients. In its latest annual report, the company noted that no single customer accounts for more than 10% of total revenue, which reduces the risk associated with relying on any one client.

In its latest annual report, filed for the fiscal year ended Jan. 31, 2026, revenue reached nearly $41.5 billion. This represents a growth rate of approximately 9.6% compared with the prior fiscal year. Net income for this period climbed to roughly $7.5 billion. This growth suggests the company is successfully upselling existing clients to more advanced tech stocks within its ecosystem.

As of its January 2026 balance sheet, the debt-to-equity ratio was approximately 0.3x. This ratio measures total debt relative to shareholders' equity, and a lower number indicates a more conservative use of borrowed money. The current ratio, which compares short-term assets to short-term liabilities, stood at roughly 0.8x. Free cash flow for the period reached close to $14.4 billion. Note that stock-based compensation accounted for roughly 23.4% of operating cash flow, inflating reported cash generation, since SBC is a non-cash expense added back to cash flow in the cash flow statement.

The case for International Business Machines

International Business Machines focuses on providing hybrid cloud infrastructure, consulting services, and enterprise AI tools. The company serves a diverse global client base, ranging from small businesses to large governments, across more than 175 countries. About 60% of its total revenue is generated outside the United States, showcasing its deep reach into international markets and its reliance on a global network of partners.

In its latest annual report, filed for the fiscal year ended Dec. 31, 2025, revenue reached nearly $67.5 billion. This was an increase of roughly 7.6% compared with the prior fiscal year. Net income for the period was approximately $10.6 billion. The growth reflects a strategic shift toward recurring software revenue and high-margin consulting contracts that help other businesses modernize their legacy technology systems.

The Zacks Consensus Estimate for third-quarter revenues is currently pegged at $4.09 billion, indicating 20% growth from the figure reported in the year-ago quarter.

Let's see how things are shaping up prior to this announcement.

NOW's Q3 to Ride on Strong Portfolio Amid Stiff Competition

ServiceNow's third-quarter 2026 results are expected to have benefited from accelerating enterprise adoption of agentic AI solutions, particularly Now Assist, AI Control Tower and Autonomous Workforce. The company's AI annual contract value (ACV) exceeded $1 billion in the second quarter, with net new AI ACV growing more than 40% sequentially. Growing AI deployments, combined with stronger customer consumption and increased adoption of higher-value AI packages, are expected to have supported subscription revenues.

NOW's new AI-native packaging strategy is expected to have boosted third-quarter performance by making AI capabilities accessible to a wider customer base. The company's Foundation, Advanced and Prime offerings allow enterprises to adopt AI based on their requirements. Increasing monetization opportunity is expected to have supported deal values and subscription growth. Moreover, sustained demand for IT Service Management (ITSM) and IT Operations Management (ITOM) solutions has been a key catalyst. In the second quarter of 2026, ITSM featured in 15 of the company's 20 largest deals, while ITOM was included in 18.

The company's expanding cybersecurity portfolio is expected to have been a significant contributor to third-quarter top-line growth. The integration of Armis and Veza strengthens NOW's capabilities in asset intelligence, identity security, vulnerability management and automated threat response. These solutions complement AI Control Tower and the existing ITSM and ITOM portfolios, creating opportunities for cross-selling. The combination is expected to have supported subscription revenues, larger enterprise contracts and greater adoption of the company's core workflow solutions.

However, ServiceNow's third-quarter subscription revenue growth is expected to have faced pressure from the timing of U.S. federal government contracts. Strong federal demand in the second quarter accelerated certain on-premises subscription revenues that would otherwise have been recognized in the third quarter. This pull-forward creates a difficult sequential comparison despite healthy underlying demand. NOW expects third-quarter subscription revenues of $3.975-$3.980 billion, indicating approximately 20% year-over-year growth in constant currency, compared with 23% growth in the second quarter.

The company's third-quarter results are expected to have suffered from unfavorable forex and acquisition-related charges. Higher AI processing requirements and cloud delivery costs are likely to have increased subscription costs. Moreover, stiff competition from Salesforce CRM, Microsoft MSFT, Oracle ORCL and other enterprise software vendors that are rapidly embedding generative AI into their platforms, requiring continued investment to sustain technological leadership, has been a headwind. This is expected to have kept margins under pressure in the to-be-reported quarter.

Investing.com — Salesforce Inc (NYSE:CRM) has staged one of enterprise tech's most decisive turnarounds. Trading near $248.11 per share, the software giant is up +52.55% since July, shaking off earlier fears that generative artificial intelligence would disintermediate enterprise SaaS platforms.

The rebound has been driven by tangible AI monetization rather than speculative promises. In its latest quarter, Salesforce reported that its Agentforce platform reached $1.5 billion in annual recurring revenue, while adjusted earnings beat consensus estimates by over 80%. Even after that sharp rally, the stock trades at just 13.9 times forward earnings with a PEG ratio of 0.37, leaving significant valuation headroom.

That combination of accelerating profitability and discounted valuation is why ProPicks AI models selected the stock for the Dominate the Dow strategy in July before adding it to the Top Value Stocks strategy in October.

In its latest rebalance, those same models flagged three new value additions alongside Salesforce—spanning industrial technology, specialized energy equipment, and consumer retail—displaying the same cash-flow durability that first signaled Salesforce's rebound.

See the three new value additions models are targeting alongside Salesforce: Explore the Top Value Stocks strategy on InvestingPro

Debunking the software disruption narrative

Earlier this year, enterprise software faced widespread skepticism as investors questioned whether generative AI would compress seat counts and erode software pricing power. That sentiment pushed Salesforce down toward 52-week lows near $146.

However, recent operating results demonstrated that enterprise software is capturing AI value at the application layer. In the second quarter, Salesforce generated record revenue of $11.35 billion, up 11% year-over-year, while operating cash flow supported an 81% surge in free cash flow to $1.1 billion. Non-GAAP operating margins expanded to 34.1%, underscoring strict cost discipline alongside growth.

Crucially, AI adoption is transitioning rapidly from experimental pilots to commercial deployment. Agentforce bookings saw triple-digit growth, with agentic workspace units surging 97% quarter-over-quarter to 3.2 billion. Rather than building models from scratch, enterprise clients are using Salesforce to deploy autonomous agents directly into sales, customer service, and marketing workflows.

Deals across the software, financial technology, and energy sectors are in focus this week as investors track strategic acquisitions and consolidations in the market.

Last week, Salesforce Inc. (CRM) said that it will acquire customer engagement platform Braze Inc. (BRZE) for about $5.66 billion in enterprise value.

Tradeweb Markets Inc. (TW), an electronic trading company, announced that it will acquire fintech company Trumid Holdings, LLC for approximately $1.97 billion.

Nuclear energy company Centrus Energy Corp. (LEU) also said last week that it completed the acquisition of Westerman Holdings, LLC, one of its largest and most diversified suppliers, for about $116 million.

Salesforce Expands Marketing Capabilities With Braze Acquisition

Under the terms of the deal, Braze Class A common stock owners are set to receive $47.50 in cash per share after the acquisition, which Salesforce expects to complete in fiscal 2028, subject to shareholder approval.

President and Chief Operating and Financial Officer Robin Washington of Salesforce noted that the purchase price represents about five times Braze's expected fiscal 2028 revenue.

The deal will be funded using cash, Salesforce said, and will not require debt financing. Salesforce President of Applications and Marketing Patrick Stokes added that the proposed acquisition is to expand Salesforce's marketing capabilities as brands look forward to more immediate, personalized interactions with customers across mobile apps, the web, email, SMS, WhatsApp and other channels.

Braze Co-Founder and Chief Executive Officer Bill Magnuson said that following the deal, it will continue to operate as 'Braze' with him as CEO within Salesforce.

Retail sentiment around CRM and BRZE stocks was 'neutral' at the time of writing.

Tradeweb's Trumid Acquisition Expands Credit Capabilities

Tradeweb Markets' agreement to acquire Trumid Holdings, LLC, a financial technology company and electronic credit trading marketplace, includes about $1.75 billion in payment for the business and about $220 million for the tax assets.

SAN FRANCISCO, October 23, 2026--(BUSINESS WIRE)--Salesforce (NYSE: CRM), the #1 AI CRM, today announced it has granted equity awards under its 2014 Inducement Equity Incentive Plan (the "Plan") to new employees who joined Salesforce in connection with the acquisition of m3ter and Fin. The Plan was adopted by the Salesforce Board of Directors in July 2014, in accordance with New York Stock Exchange Rule 303A.08.

Under the Plan, Salesforce granted a total of 278,068 restricted stock units ("RSUs") to 28 employees at m3ter and 6 employees at Fin. These RSUs vest over four years, with 25% vesting on the first anniversary of the grant date, and the remaining 75% of the RSUs vesting quarterly thereafter in 12 equal installments.

All equity awards are subject to the employee's continued service through each applicable vesting date. Each of the employees who received an award is a non-executive officer.
